cards.question: What does a Mutex guarantee?
cards.answer: Mutual exclusion: it works as an exclusive reference, so only one thread can hold the lock at a time.

cards.question: How does Mutex conflicting access differ from RefCell?
cards.answer: Unlike RefCell, conflicting access does not panic. The waiting thread is put to sleep and woken when the lock is dropped so it can try to take a reference.

cards.question: Why does Mutex have no unlock method?
cards.answer: lock returns a MutexGuard that accesses the data as an exclusive reference through DerefMut. Dropping the guard frees the lock via Drop.

cards.question: In the 10-thread increment example, what does each thread observe?
cards.answer: Each of the 10 threads increments 100 times. Each thread sees the count as 0, 100, 200, through 900, runs, then drops the guard, for a final value of 1000.
